newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 9.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Korean newspapers - May 9.

text.p: The following is a summary of major stories in leading South Korean newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy.
- Hanbo Group president Chung Tae-soo told prosecutors he gave 90 billion won to Kim Young-sam during the 1992 presidential election campaign.

- Yielding to mounting pressure from the U.S. and the European Union (EU), which attacked Korea's frugality campaign as an anti-import drive, the government has decided to officially declare its nondiscriminatory policy on imports.
- All phone call charges will be liberalized probably in October.
- The government is willing to offer aid desired by North Korea if delivery made through Panmunjom.

- President Kim Young-sam on Thursday banned presidential hopefuls in the ruling New Korea Party from challenging to NKP chairman Rep. Lee Hoi-chang, apparently lending his absolute support to Lee, who is now besieged by rival contenders for the nomination.
- National Congress for New Politics Party asserted that president Kim Young-sam is at the center of the Hanbo loans scandal and he will have to assume responsibility for it.
